stage1.impression: A clean, quiet catalogue render: the ice-blue resin horn is the best thing in the frame, glowing and well edged, and the cabinet's tint reads true. But it still reads as CG: the cabinet barely touches the paper (a soft, shallow shadow with no dark core), the top of the cabinet and the horn's right rim dissolve into a near-white background, the paper falls off in an uneven diagonal from a grey top-left corner, and the flat matte cloth disc and blocky white lining look like untextured placeholders.

blocking_9: A grounded contact: a dark core line under the cabinet's front edge and a shadow that falls off over about 10 cm, so the speaker has visible weight
The cabinet's top face and the horn's right rim separate from the paper by at least 15 levels of luminance
The paper reads as one even, deliberate gradient, with no grey wedge in one corner
The cloth disc and the lining show real textile micro-texture (out of scope here, but it holds the image under 9)
The acrylic front panel carries at least one long, soft specular sheen so it reads as a glossy 20 mm slab rather than a tinted outline

defects.what: Contact shadow weak: the paper right under the front edge measures lum 176 against 194 to 211 just below it; no dark core, so the cabinet looks set on, not standing
Grey wedge in the top-left corner (lum about 175) against 236 at top right: an uneven diagonal falloff that reads as an unlit corner of the sweep, not a choice
Background behind the horn's right rim and the cabinet's right side is 242, near white; the horn's bright rim and the cabinet's top edge merge into it
Cabinet top face almost invisible: pale against pale paper, only a thin grey line marks the top-front edge
Lining inside the top band clips in the blue channel (b 250, clip 0.77 percent): a flat, blown white
Cloth disc is a flat, uniform matte blue (lum range 20) with no weave: reads as a plastic disc (out of scope)
Lining batts read as smooth white boxes, no fibre or voile texture (out of scope)
Front acrylic face has no broad sheen; the slab reads only through its dark edges
